extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, trial judges, outside and in-house counsel, and testifying/non-testifying experts involved in patent litigation
extracted.subtask_short: drafting protective order in patent litigation
extracted.subtask_description: Model Stipulated Protective Order provisions and procedural guidance for handling Confidential, Highly Confidential – Attorneys' Eyes Only, and Source Code materials in patent litigation, including disclosure limits, inspection protocols, prosecution bars, subpoena and non-party procedures, and final disposition requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet-and-confer and motion requirements for disclosure to Designated House Counsel or Experts
rubrics_metrics.description: A Party that receives a timely written objection must meet and confer with the Designating Party (through direct voice to voice dialogue) to try to resolve the matter by agreement within seven days of the written objection. If no agreement is reached, the Party seeking to make the disclosure ... may file a motion ... seeking permission from the court to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The motion must describe the circumstances with specificity, set forth in detail the reasons why the disclosure is reasonably necessary, assess the risk of harm that the disclosure would entail, and suggest additional means to reduce that risk. It must be accompanied by a competent declaration describing the parties' efforts to resolve the matter by agreement and the reasons advanced by the Designating Party for its refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof when opposing disclosure to Designated House Counsel or Experts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Party opposing disclosure to Designated House Counsel or the Expert shall bear the burden of proving that the risk of harm that the disclosure would entail (under the safeguards proposed) outweighs the Receiving Party’s need to disclose the Protected Material to its Designated House Counsel or Expert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution bar (scope and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent written consent from the Producing Party, any individual who receives access to 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS' EYES ONLY' [Optional: or 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – SOURCE CODE'] information shall not be involved in the prosecution of patents or patent applications relating to [insert subject matter ...], including without limitation the patents asserted in this action and any patent or application claiming priority to or otherwise related to the patents asserted in this action, before any foreign or domestic agency, including the United States Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of this paragraph, 'prosecution' includes directly or indirectly drafting, amending, advising, or otherwise affecting the scope or maintenance of patent claims. 'Prosecution' does not include representing a party challenging a patent before a domestic or foreign agency (e.g., reissue protest, ex parte reexamination or inter partes reexamination). The Prosecution Bar begins when access is first received and ends two (2) years after final termination of the action (unless alternative language is used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical wall option for counsel who receive AEO information
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be appropriate under certain circumstances to require Outside and House Counsel who receive access to 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS’ EYES ONLY' information to implement an 'Ethical Wall.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court or parties may include an Ethical Wall requirement where appropriate to reduce risk of improper use of AEO information; specific implementation details should be negotiated or ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source code designation authority
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent production of source code becomes necessary ... a Producing Party may designate source code as 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL - SOURCE CODE' if it comprises or includes confidential, proprietary or trade secret source code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source code protections and permitted recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Protected Material designated as 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – SOURCE CODE' shall be subject to all of the protections afforded to 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS’ EYES ONLY' information [Optional: including the Prosecution Bar], and may be disclosed only to the individuals to whom 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS’ EYES ONLY' information may be disclosed, as set forth in Paragraphs 7.3 and 7.4, with the exception of Designated House Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may tailor exceptions (e.g., permitting certain House Counsel access to derivative materials) depending on circumstances; such exceptions should be explicitly enumerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source code inspection environment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any source code produced in discovery shall be made available for inspection, in a format allowing it to be reasonably reviewed and searched, during normal business hours or at other mutually agreeable times, at an office of the Producing Party’s counsel or another mutually agreed upon location. The source code shall be made available for inspection on a secured computer in a secured room without Internet access or network access to other computers, and the Receiving Party shall not copy, remove, or otherwise transfer any portion of the source code onto any recordable media or recordable device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Producing Party may visually monitor the activities of the Receiving Party’s representatives during any source code review, but only to ensure that there is no unauthorized recording, copying, or transmission of the source code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producing Party's right to monitor inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Producing Party may visually monitor the activities of the Receiving Party’s representatives during any source code review, but only to ensure that there is no unauthorized recording, copying, or transmission of the source code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring is limited to preventing unauthorized recording/copying/transmission; it should not be used to observe substantive review beyond that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper copies of limited portions of source code (when allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Receiving Party may request paper copies of limited portions of source code that are reasonably necessary for the preparation of court filings, pleadings, expert reports, or other papers, or for deposition or trial, but shall not request paper copies for the purposes of reviewing the source code other than electronically in the first instance. The Producing Party shall provide all such source code in paper form including bates numbers and the label 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL - SOURCE CODE.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Producing Party may challenge the amount of source code requested in hard copy via the dispute resolution procedure; paper copies should be narrowly tailored to what is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on handling paper copies of source code
rubrics_metrics.description: The Receiving Party shall maintain a record of any individual who has inspected any portion of the source code in electronic or paper form. The Receiving Party shall maintain all paper copies of any printed portions of the source code in a secured, locked area. The Receiving Party shall not create any electronic or other images of the paper copies and shall not convert any of the information contained in the paper copies into any electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional paper copies allowed only if necessary for court filings, deposition, or preparation. Any paper copies used during a deposition shall be retrieved by the Producing Party at the end of each day and must not be given to or left with a court reporter or any other unauthorized individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping/logging of source code inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be appropriate under certain circumstances to require the Receiving Party to keep a paper log indicating the names of any individuals inspecting the source code and dates and times of inspection, and the names of any individuals to whom paper copies of portions of source code are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log requirements may be imposed to ensure traceability and accountability for access to highly sensitive source code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate inspection location or format where parties/counsel are in different jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative: Any source code produced in discovery shall be made available for inspection in a format through which it could be reasonably reviewed and searched during normal business hours or other mutually agreeable times at a location that is reasonably convenient for the Receiving Party and any experts to whom the source code may be disclosed. This alternative may be appropriate if the Producing Party and/or its counsel are located in a different jurisdiction than counsel and/or experts for the Receiving Party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should negotiate a convenient inspection protocol that preserves security while avoiding undue burden due to geographic distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected material subpoenaed or ordered produced in other litigation (notice and cooperation duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Party is served with a subpoena or a court order issued in other litigation that compels disclosure of any information or items designated in this action as 'CONFIDENTIAL' or 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS’ EYES ONLY' [Optional: or 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – SOURCE CODE'] that Party must: (a) promptly notify in writing the Designating Party (include copy of subpoena or order); (b) promptly notify in writing the party who caused the subpoena or order to issue in the other litigation that some or all of the material covered by the subpoena or order is subject to this Protective Order (include copy of this Stipulated Protective Order); and (c) cooperate with respect to all reasonable procedures sought by the Designating Party whose Protected Material may be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Designating Party timely seeks a protective order, the Party served shall not produce any information designated here before a determination by the issuing court, unless it has obtained the Designating Party’s permission. The Designating Party bears the burden and expense of seeking protection in that court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Party’s protected material produced in this litigation (notice and inspection procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms of this Order are applicable to information produced by a Non-Party in this action and designated as 'CONFIDENTIAL' or 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS’ EYES ONLY' ... If a Party is required, by a valid discovery request, to produce a Non-Party’s confidential information in its possession, and the Party is subject to an agreement with the Non-Party not to produce the Non-Party’s confidential information, then the Party shall: (1) promptly notify in writing the Requesting Party and the Non-Party; (2) promptly provide the Non-Party with a copy of the Stipulated Protective Order, the relevant discovery request(s), and a reasonably specific description of the information requested; and (3) make the information requested available for inspection by the Non-Party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Non-Party fails to object or seek a protective order within 14 days, the Receiving Party may produce the Non-Party’s confidential information. If the Non-Party timely seeks protection, the Receiving Party shall not produce before a court determination. Absent court order to the contrary, the Non-Party bears the burden and expense of seeking protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized disclosure response obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Receiving Party learns that, by inadvertence or otherwise, it has disclosed Protected Material to any person or in any circumstance not authorized under this Stipulated Protective Order, the Receiving Party must immediately (a) notify in writing the Designating Party of the unauthorized disclosures, (b) use its best efforts to retrieve all unauthorized copies of the Protected Material, (c) inform the person or persons to whom unauthorized disclosures were made of all the terms of this Order, and (d) request such person or persons to execute the 'Acknowledgment and Agreement to Be Bound'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt, proactive remedial actions are required to mitigate harm and preserve confidentiality; documentation of retrieval efforts is advisable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent production of privileged or protected material
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Producing Party gives notice to Receiving Parties that certain inadvertently produced material is subject to a claim of privilege or other protection, the obligations of the Receiving Parties are those set forth in Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(b)(5)(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may agree to alternate procedures; the order contemplates incorporation of Federal Rule of Evidence 502(d) and (e) to define effects of disclosure. An alternative provision could require return/destroy and prohibit sequester/use until claim resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to seek further relief and preserve other objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Order abridges the right of any person to seek its modification by the court in the future. By stipulating to the entry of this Protective Order no Party waives any right it otherwise would have to object to disclosing or producing any information or item on any ground not addressed in this Stipulated Protective Order. Similarly, no Party waives any right to object on any ground to use in evidence of any of the material covered by this Protective Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional export control compliance provision
rubrics_metrics.description: [Optional: Export Control. Disclosure of Protected Material shall be subject to all applicable laws and regulations relating to the export of technical data contained in such Protected Material, including the release of such technical data to foreign persons or nationals in the United States or elsewhere. The Producing Party shall be responsible for identifying any such controlled technical data, and the Receiving Party shall take measures necessary to ensure compliance.]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, parties should identify export-controlled materials and adopt procedures to prevent unlawful transfer to foreign persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Protected Material under seal (requirements and standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Without written permission from the Designating Party or a court order secured after appropriate notice to all interested persons, a Party may not file in the public record in this action any Protected Material. A Party that seeks to file under seal any Protected Material must comply with Civil Local Rule 79-5. Protected Material may only be filed under seal pursuant to a court order authorizing the sealing of the specific Protected Material at issue. Pursuant to Civil Local Rule 79-5, a sealing order will issue only upon a request establishing that the Protected Material at issue is privileged, protectable as a trade secret, or otherwise entitled to protection under the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request to file under seal is denied, the Receiving Party may file the Protected Material in the public record pursuant to applicable local rules unless otherwise instructed by the court. Filing under seal generally requires a public redacted version unless excused by court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final disposition: return/destruction and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after the final disposition of this action ... each Receiving Party must return all Protected Material to the Producing Party or destroy such material. 'All Protected Material' includes all copies, abstracts, compilations, summaries, and any other format reproducing or capturing any of the Protected Material. Whether returned or destroyed, the Receiving Party must submit a written certification to the Producing Party ... that (1) identifies (by category, where appropriate) all the Protected Material that was returned or destroyed and (2) affirms that the Receiving Party has not retained any copies, abstracts, compilations, summaries or any other format reproducing or capturing any of the Protected Material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel are entitled to retain archival copies of pleadings, transcripts, legal memoranda, exhibits, expert reports, attorney work product, and consultant/expert work product even if those materials contain Protected Material; those archival copies remain subject to the Protective Order (duration provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit A: Acknowledgment and Agreement to be Bound (requirements for persons granted access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who will receive access to Protected Material must sign an Acknowledgment and Agreement to Be Bound (Exhibit A) declaring they have read and understand the Stipulated Protective Order, agree to comply with and be bound by its terms, acknowledge potential sanctions for noncompliance, and submit to the jurisdiction of the issuing court for enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Acknowledgment form also requires the signee to appoint an agent for service of process (e.g., California agent) and to provide identifying information (name, address, etc.). Parties must retain executed undertakings and serve copies on other parties per the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and designation procedures for Confidential and Highly Confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: 'Confidential' information is information concerning business operations, processes, and technical and development information ... disclosure of which is likely to harm competitive position. 'Highly Confidential' information is trade secrets and plans more sensitive or strategic than Confidential information, the disclosure of which is likely to significantly harm competitive position. Designation: designate by clearly marking on its face as 'CONFIDENTIAL' or 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL'; deposition designations may be made on the record or in writing within 14 days after receipt of the transcript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A failure to designate does not constitute forfeiture of a claim of confidentiality as to other materials. A designating person may withdraw a designation by written notification. If a party disputes a designation, it must notify the producer in writing identifying specific documents and propose a new designation; parties must meet and confer; unless producer moves to maintain the designation within 14 days, the proposed new designation will be applied. The producer bears the burden to prove the designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and disclosure limits and authorized recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential and Highly Confidential information may be used exclusively for purposes of this litigation. Absent written permission or further court order, recipients may not disclose Confidential information except to: (i) a party’s outside counsel of record and necessary staff; (ii) a party’s in-house counsel; (iii) a party’s officers and employees directly involved in this case; (iv) stenographer/videographer; (v) experts/consultants and their staff (subject to undertaking); and (vi) the Court and court personnel. Highly Confidential may be disclosed only to a subset (i), (iv), (v), and (vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure to experts/consultants requires execution of an undertaking (Appendix 1) and serving the undertaking on other parties within ten days. At least ten days before first disclosure to an expert/consultant, the disclosing party must serve the producer with the expert’s ID and CV; the producer has ten days to object for good cause (not including qualifications); unresolved disputes require court resolution before disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to confidentiality restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding restrictions, a party may disclose Confidential or Highly Confidential information to: (i) any employee or author of the producer; (ii) any person, no longer affiliated with the producer, who authored the information in whole or in part; and (iii) any person who received the information before this case was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure to other persons not authorized requires a reasonable attempt to obtain producer’s permission, or else a court motion for permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies, production, and disposal of materials during and after litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: A party producing documents must, upon request, furnish the requesting party with one copy at the requesting party’s expense (parties must agree on copying rates). Upon conclusion of the case, each party must return to the producer all documents and copies containing the producer’s Confidential or Highly Confidential information, and must destroy notes, memoranda, or other materials derived from or revealing such information. Alternatively, with producer’s agreement, the party may destroy materials and certify compliance. Parties and counsel may retain one complete set of all documents filed with the Court, subject to the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legible photocopy may be used as the 'original' for all purposes; actual originals must be made available within ten days after written request. Obligations regarding Confidential/Highly Confidential information survive the case conclusion.
